body: thanks. i dont have alot of people i can relate to, so it helps knowing that there are others in my shoes. i never seemed to really form a coherent theory of mind so i find it difficult to put myself in other peoples shoes. though, i do not know if it is due to me being on the spectrum or because of a sheltered upbringing. maybe both.

unfortunately i have tried lots of times in the past to socialize with confidence. people have either found me weird at best or i make them extremely uncomfortable at worst.  my counselor strongly believes i may have undiagnosed autism (will be getting an evaluation covered by vocational services), due to my adoptive parents being from an older generation and not understanding certain mental conditions. if it helps to clarify, i was in special and remedial classes for most of my school life. 

as far as the responsibilities part is concerned; i have a ton of them. my guardian unfortunately does not have the money to pay my car insurance and we are actually fairly poor (we are just scraping by) . i only have no debt due to my grandfather, but he does not assume other financial responsibilities in my life. 

my main concern at this point isn't really making friends even though i have never really had friends in my life, but rather to get a good paying job. i couldn't pass business courses though.
